1	# Centered factorial effects and equivalent Gaussian parameterizations
2	
3	This offline packet contains the statistical definitions needed to interpret
4	the supplied calibration workflow. It is based on the version-matched PyMC
5	distribution documentation, the PyMC3 framework paper, and the Stan User's
6	Guide discussion of centered vectors.
7	
8	## 1. Factorial calibration model
9	
10	Suppose laboratories `l = 1, ..., L` measure the same response under protocols
11	`p = 1, ..., P`. A two-way Gaussian effects model can be written as
12	
13	$$
14	y_{lp} \sim
15	\mathcal{N}(\mu + a_l + b_p + g_{lp}, s_{lp}),
16	$$
17	
18	where `mu` is the grand mean, `a_l` is a laboratory effect, `b_p` is a
19	protocol effect, `g_lp` is a laboratory-by-protocol interaction, and `s_lp`
20	is the known standard error of the observed cell summary.
21	
22	Without identifying constraints, constants can be moved between the grand mean
23	and the main effects without changing fitted responses. A common convention is
24	
25	$$
26	\sum_{l=1}^{L} a_l = 0,
27	\qquad
28	\sum_{p=1}^{P} b_p = 0.
29	$$
30	
31	The interaction represents only the non-additive part of the response when it
32	is centered across both axes:
33	
34	$$
35	\sum_{l=1}^{L} g_{lp} = 0 \quad \text{for every } p,
36	\qquad
37	\sum_{p=1}^{P} g_{lp} = 0 \quad \text{for every } l.
38	$$
39	
40	These constraints define the interpretation of the effects. They are not
41	additional observations.
42	
43	## 2. Documented centered Gaussian distribution
44	
45	The source-version PyMC documentation describes `ZeroSumNormal` as a centered
46	Gaussian distribution for which one or more selected trailing axes sum to zero.
47	For one constrained axis of length `K`, the covariance is
48	
49	$$
50	\operatorname{Cov}(x) =
51	\sigma^2\left(I - \frac{1}{K}J\right),
52	$$
53	
54	where `I` is the identity matrix and every entry of `J` is one. The parameter
55	`sigma` is the standard deviation of the underlying unconstrained Normal used
56	by the construction. In this source version it is a positive scalar.
57	
58	By default the rightmost axis is constrained. The public API can constrain more
59	than one trailing axis. A matrix constrained over its last two axes therefore
60	has zero sums along both of those axes.
61	
62	## 3. Orthonormal reduced coordinates
63	
64	A zero-sum vector can be represented without redundancy. Let the columns of
65	`B` form an orthonormal basis for the subspace perpendicular to the all-ones
66	vector:
67	
68	$$
69	B^T B = I,
70	\qquad
71	B^T \mathbf{1} = 0.
72	$$
73	
74	If
75	
76	$$
77	z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 I),
78	\qquad
79	x = Bz,
80	$$
81	
82	then `x` has the centered covariance above and lies on the zero-sum support.
83	Subtracting the mean from an unconstrained Gaussian vector is another way to
84	construct the same covariance.
85	
86	For a two-way interaction, bases for the laboratory and protocol centered
87	subspaces can be combined to represent exactly the matrices whose row and
88	column sums are zero.
89	
90	## 4. Reparameterization coherence
91	
92	A full constrained representation and an orthonormal reduced-coordinate
93	representation are two coordinate systems for the same statistical model. In a
94	linear-Gaussian analysis with the same priors, observations, and standard
95	errors, they must produce the same posterior fitted responses and the same
96	posterior summaries for any fixed linear contrast, up to numerical and Monte
97	Carlo error.
98	
99	This statement does not depend on a particular optimizer or sampler. Different
100	computational paths may represent the model differently internally, but they do
101	not define different prior shrinkage or different scientific contrasts.
102	
103	## 5. Planned interaction contrasts
104	
105	A difference-in-differences contrast compares a protocol change between two
106	laboratories. For laboratories `l_1`, `l_2` and protocols `p_1`, `p_2`,
107	one example is
108	
109	$$
110	C =
111	(\eta_{l_1 p_1} - \eta_{l_1 p_2})
112	-
113	(\eta_{l_2 p_1} - \eta_{l_2 p_2}),
114	$$
115	
116	where `eta_lp = mu + a_l + b_p + g_lp` is the fitted response. Additive grand,
117	laboratory, and protocol contributions cancel, so this contrast isolates a
118	laboratory-by-protocol interaction.
119	
120	Posterior means estimate the interaction contrast. Posterior standard
121	deviations and intervals quantify uncertainty. Both are properties of the
122	declared probability model.
123	
124	## 6. Sources
125	
126	- Salvatier, Wiecki, and Fonnesbeck, "Probabilistic programming in Python using
127	  PyMC3," *PeerJ Computer Science* 2:e55 (2016), DOI
128	  [10.7717/peerj-cs.55](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.55).
129	- PyMC documentation, `ZeroSumNormal` distribution API:
130	  [pymc.ZeroSumNormal](https://www.pymc.io/projects/docs/en/stable/api/distributions/generated/pymc.ZeroSumNormal.html).
131	- Stan User's Guide, "Parameterizing centered vectors":
132	  [centered-vector parameterization](https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/regression.html#parameterizing-centered-vectors).
133	- Matching source-version documentation is retained in
134	  `source/pymc/distributions/multivariate.py`.
135	
136	These sources define the support, covariance, parameter meaning, model
137	identifiability, and equivalence needed for the investigation. They do not
138	prescribe a source-level repair.

    Constrains any random samples to sum to zero along the user-provided ``zerosum_axes``.

    Parameters

    zerosum_axes : list of ints

def extend_axis(array, axis):
    n = array.shape[axis] + 1
    sum_vals = array.sum(axis, keepdims=True)
    norm = sum_vals / (pt.sqrt(n) + n)
    fill_val = norm - sum_vals / pt.sqrt(n)

    out = pt.concatenate([array, fill_val], axis=axis)
    return out - norm


def extend_axis_rev(array, axis):
    normalized_axis = normalize_axis_tuple(axis, array.ndim)[0]

    n = array.shape[normalized_axis]

    norm = sum_vals / (pt.sqrt(n) + n)

    _full_size = pt.prod(shape)

        pm.logp(normal_dist, value) * _degrees_of_freedom / _full_size,

        # "stabilization", as well as "HEAD" and "master".

            print("discarding '%s', no digits" % ",".join(refs - tags))

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from pymc.distributions.transforms import extend_axis

labs = case['laboratories']; protos = case['protocols']
L=len(labs); P=len(protos)

se = np.array(case['cell_standard_errors'], dtype=float)
sc = case['prior_scales']
sampling = case['sampling']

def summarize_posterior(idata, contrast):
    post=idata.posterior
    mu=post['grand_mean'].values
    a=post['laboratory_effect'].values
    b=post['protocol_effect'].values
    g=post['interaction_effect'].values
    eta=mu[...,None,None]+a[...,:,None]+b[...,None,:]+g
    vals=np.zeros(eta.shape[:2])
    for term in contrast['terms']:
        vals += term['coefficient']*eta[..., term['laboratory_index'], term['protocol_index']]
    vals=vals.reshape(-1)
    return float(np.mean(vals)), float(np.std(vals, ddof=1))

# Model A: public ZeroSumNormal
with pm.Model():
    mu = pm.Normal('grand_mean', mu=0., sigma=sc['grand_mean'])
    a = pm.ZeroSumNormal('laboratory_effect', sigma=sc['laboratory'], shape=L)
    b = pm.ZeroSumNormal('protocol_effect', sigma=sc['protocol'], shape=P)
    g = pm.ZeroSumNormal('interaction_effect', sigma=sc['interaction'], shape=(L,P), n_zerosum_axes=2)
    eta = mu + a[:,None] + b[None,:] + g
    pm.Normal('obs', mu=eta, sigma=se, observed=y)
    idataA = pm.sample(draws=sampling['draws'], tune=sampling['tune'], chains=1, cores=1,
                       random_seed=sampling['seed'], target_accept=sampling['target_accept'],
                       progressbar=False, compute_convergence_checks=False, discard_tuned_samples=True,
                       return_inferencedata=True)

# Model B: reduced coordinates via extend_axis
with pm.Model():
    mu = pm.Normal('grand_mean', mu=0., sigma=sc['grand_mean'])
    za = pm.Normal('za', 0., sc['laboratory'], shape=(L-1,))
    zb = pm.Normal('zb', 0., sc['protocol'], shape=(P-1,))
    zg = pm.Normal('zg', 0., sc['interaction'], shape=(L-1,P-1))
    a = pm.Deterministic('laboratory_effect', extend_axis(za, axis=0))
    b = pm.Deterministic('protocol_effect', extend_axis(zb, axis=0))
    g_raw = extend_axis(zg, axis=-2)
    g = pm.Deterministic('interaction_effect', extend_axis(g_raw, axis=-1))
    eta = mu + a[:,None] + b[None,:] + g
    pm.Normal('obs', mu=eta, sigma=se, observed=y)
    idataB = pm.sample(draws=sampling['draws'], tune=sampling['tune'], chains=1, cores=1,
                       random_seed=sampling['seed'], target_accept=sampling['target_accept'],
                       progressbar=False, compute_convergence_checks=False, discard_tuned_samples=True,
                       return_inferencedata=True)

for c in case['planned_contrasts']:
    print(c['name'], 'A', summarize_posterior(idataA, c), 'B', summarize_posterior(idataB, c))

def check_parameters(

    """Wrap an expression in a CheckParameterValue that asserts several conditions are met.

def get_support_shape(
    support_shape: Optional[Sequence[Union[int, np.ndarray, TensorVariable]]],
    *,
    shape: Optional[Shape] = None,
    dims: Optional[Dims] = None,
    observed: Optional[Any] = None,
    support_shape_offset: Sequence[int] = None,
    ndim_supp: int = 1,
) -> Optional[TensorVariable]:
    """Extract the support shapes from shape / dims / observed information

    Parameters
    ----------
    support_shape:
        User-specified support shape for multivariate distribution
    shape:
        User-specified shape for multivariate distribution
    dims:
        User-specified dims for multivariate distribution
    observed:
        User-specified observed data from multivariate distribution
    support_shape_offset:
        Difference between last shape dimensions and the length of
        explicit support shapes in multivariate distribution, defaults to 0.
        For timeseries, this is shape[-1] = support_shape[-1] + 1
    ndim_supp:
        Number of support dimensions of the given multivariate distribution, defaults to 1

    Returns
    -------
    support_shape
        Support shape, if specified directly by user, or inferred from the last dimensions of
        shape / dims / observed. When two sources of support shape information are provided,
        a symbolic Assert is added to ensure they are consistent.
    """
    if ndim_supp < 1:
        raise NotImplementedError("ndim_supp must be bigger than 0")
    if support_shape_offset is None:
        support_shape_offset = [0] * ndim_supp
    elif isinstance(support_shape_offset, int):
        support_shape_offset = [support_shape_offset] * ndim_supp
    inferred_support_shape: Optional[Sequence[Union[int, np.ndarray, Variable]]] = None

    if shape is not None:
        shape = to_tuple(shape)
        assert isinstance(shape, tuple)
        if len(shape) < ndim_supp:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Number of shape dimensions is too small for ndim_supp of {ndim_supp}"
            )
        inferred_support_shape = [
            shape[i] - support_shape_offset[i] for i in np.arange(-ndim_supp, 0)
        ]

    if inferred_support_shape is None and dims is not None:
        dims = convert_dims(dims)
        assert isinstance(dims, tuple)
        if len(dims) < ndim_supp:
            raise ValueError(f"Number of dims is too small for ndim_supp of {ndim_supp}")
        model = modelcontext(None)
        inferred_support_shape = [
            model.dim_lengths[dims[i]] - support_shape_offset[i]  # type: ignore
            for i in np.arange(-ndim_supp, 0)
        ]

    if inferred_support_shape is None and observed is not None:
        observed = convert_observed_data(observed)
        if observed.ndim < ndim_supp:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Number of observed dimensions is too small for ndim_supp of {ndim_supp}"
            )
        inferred_support_shape = [
            observed.shape[i] - support_shape_offset[i] for i in np.arange(-ndim_supp, 0)
        ]

    if inferred_support_shape is None:
        if support_shape is not None:
            # Only source of information was the originally provided support_shape
            inferred_support_shape = support_shape
        else:
            # We did not learn anything
            return None
    elif support_shape is not None:
        # There were two sources of support_shape, make sure they are consistent
        inferred_support_shape = [
            cast(
                Variable,
                Assert(msg="support_shape does not match respective shape dimension")(
                    inferred, pt.eq(inferred, explicit)
                ),
            )
            for inferred, explicit in zip(inferred_support_shape, support_shape)
        ]

    return pt.stack(inferred_support_shape)


def get_support_shape_1d(
    support_shape: Optional[Union[int, np.ndarray, TensorVariable]],
    *,
    shape: Optional[Shape] = None,
    dims: Optional[Dims] = None,
    observed: Optional[Any] = None,
    support_shape_offset: int = 0,
) -> Optional[TensorVariable]:
    """Helper function for cases when you just care about one dimension."""
    support_shape_tuple = get_support_shape(
        support_shape=(support_shape,) if support_shape is not None else None,
        shape=shape,
        dims=dims,
        observed=observed,
        support_shape_offset=(support_shape_offset,),
    )

    if support_shape_tuple is not None:
        (support_shape_,) = support_shape_tuple
        return support_shape_
    else:
        return None
